findings.gate: Craft core reader-trust invariant 3 (continuity persistence); charter §1 (drafted prose governs) — introduced by the repair to finding 005

draft_evidence.quote: Fifty-three, or near it, and the winter and three hundred miles had put more on him than the two years since a room in Ostrand had.

comparison_evidence.quote: He was eighteen, witnessed — the date written into the log in his own hand at the table, per the custom now three birthdays old, the smallest of the three and, though only the term suspected it, the last that would ever be kept inside an institution's walls: *Eighteen. Written at Halcenvane, in the residence common room, third month of the winter term, ninth day. Witnesses: four of my own and a cohort captain who thinks he's here for cake.*

findings.consequence: The number in the sentence is now right and the interval in the same sentence is not. The room in Ostrand is book-06 chapter-17, which falls after Cael's eighteenth birthday at chapter-14.md:119. His nineteenth is on the hundred and second day past the Line (state-b8-pre-ch01.md:3), which fixes the crossing at two hundred and sixty-three days after that birthday, and this chapter is the two hundred and seventy-seventh day. The interval from Ostrand to this landing is therefore at most five hundred and forty days — seventeen and a half months — and that is the ceiling reached only if the cache meeting sat on the birthday itself. book-06 chapter-16.md:139 dates the analysis at 'the petition was four months old' against chapter-14's 'third month of the winter term, ninth day', which puts the real figure near four hundred and eighty days, about sixteen months. 'Two years' is unreachable under the drafted timeline. The damage is that it lands in the arrival catalogue, in the one voice in the series whose authority is that its counts are right, in the same sentence the repair was fixing an arithmetic error in — so a reader who checks the first number and finds it corrected now checks the second and finds it wrong. The r1 report's own consequence text for finding 005 asserts 'roughly two years have passed', so the author imported the figure in good faith; the coordinator should treat this as a correction to the r1 report as much as to the draft.
findings.repair_target: Drop the interval or make it true. The clause does its work without a number — 'and the winter and three hundred miles had put more on him than the years since Ostrand had' — and if a figure is wanted, 'the year and a half' or 'the sixteen months' both fit the drafted timeline. Do not touch 'Fifty-three, or near it', which is correct, or the rest of the catalogue, which finding 005 protected. Note that the same edit is the cheapest place to fix finding 015 as well, since removing 'three hundred miles' from this clause returns the phrase to four.

findings.gate: Craft core reader-trust invariant 3 (continuity persistence); charter §1 (drafted prose governs) — introduced by the parallel repair to finding 004

draft_evidence.quote: She had watched Cael measured by men in grey since Norhold. She had stood in a hall at sixteen while a marshal read a page about him, and at a table at seventeen while the same man declined to read one, and she had a face for men in grey that she had never once had to use on a man out of it, and she used it now, on a brown coat, and it did not fit, and she stood in the door with the bucket and let it not fit.

comparison_evidence.quote: Lira was at the wing gate at the third bell, standing with her weight off the leading hip in a way she plainly believed nobody could see.

findings.consequence: In r1 this clause read 'a hall at fifteen', which pointed at nothing and was merely vague. The repair moved it to sixteen for consistency with the ledger at :7, which anchors it on Book 4's inspection — and Book 4's inspection is drafted, so the claim is now checkable and fails twice. Lira is not in either room. At the demonstration hall she is at the wing gate before it and gone when Cael goes in (chapter-21.md:47, and the room's occupants are itemised at :77-:79: counsel, Ilsev, Havel, Gault, the two instructors, the clerk, Vastin). At the east-room inspection she is on the bench in the common room beforehand (chapter-22.md:39, :71) and asks 'That's it?' afterwards (:279); the room is twelve feet by fourteen with five chairs and Cael counts four occupied as he enters (:77-:79). Nor does Vastin read a page in either: 'with nothing on his lap and nothing in his hands and no case anywhere near him' (chapter-21.md:77) and 'Vastin had written none of it down, because there was nothing on the table in front of him and there never had been' (chapter-22.md:205) — the empty hands are Book 4's deliberate motif for him, and the sentence spends it backwards. The second half fails the same way: book-05 chapter-23.md:45 puts the table at seventeen in a borrowed tournament administration room where Vastin stands at the window 'no aides, no case, no papers of any kind' and the scene runs on 'neither man', with Lira in the council before it and after it, not in it. The paragraph also argues with its own first sentence, which says she has watched this 'since Norhold' — Book 5's venue, after Book 4's inspection.
findings.repair_target: Give Lira the encounters she actually had, or stop placing her in rooms. The paragraph's real claim — that she has a face for men in grey and it does not fit a brown coat — needs no ledger at all, and cutting from 'She had stood' to 'declined to read one' leaves 'She had watched Cael measured by men in grey since Norhold, and she had a face for men in grey…' standing clean and true. If the two-beat cadence is wanted, place her where the prose puts her: 'She had waited at a wing gate at sixteen while he was measured, and outside a room at seventeen while he was not.' Do not touch :7, which finding 004 repaired correctly, and do not touch :73, which is the load-bearing beat of the paragraph that follows.

findings.gate: Voice charter §9 (any repeated beat phrase capped) and §8.2.3 (a tic is not a motif — the repetition's job must be recorded before the third use)

draft_evidence.quote: Fifty-three, or near it, and the winter and three hundred miles had put more on him than the two years since a room in Ostrand had. The hair gone from iron to something with less iron in it. A traveling coat, brown, road-made, the kind a carter's factor wears, with the elbows already through and the hem cut short for mud. Boots that had been good boots a long way west of here and had done three hundred miles since.

comparison_evidence.quote: Fifty-six, or near it. The hair gone from iron to something with less iron in it. A traveling coat, brown, road-made, the kind a carter's factor wears, with the elbows already through and the hem cut short for mud. Boots that had been good boots a long way west of here and had done three hundred miles since.

findings.consequence: 'Three hundred miles' ran four times in r1 — :23, :95, :101, :127 — and the r1 report recorded it as a concern rather than a finding on the §8.2.3 motif defence: each use belonged to a different speaker doing a different job, Cael cataloguing, Vastin owning, Brom pricing, Oryn finding. The repair adds a fifth, and the fifth breaks the defence, because it is the same narrator using the phrase twice inside one paragraph — once in the added clause and once thirty words later in 'had done three hundred miles since'. Two uses in one paragraph is verbatim repetition, not a motif with four owners, and §8.2.3 protects only repetition whose job is named in the arc document before the third use, which this one is not. The phrase also had zero book-level headroom before the repair; Ch4 walks the border road and will want it.
findings.repair_target: Cut the phrase from the added clause, not from the boots. 'and the winter and the road had put more on him' keeps the sentence's work and returns the chapter to four, which restores the r1 position exactly. If the coordinator wants the motif protected properly rather than trimmed, enter it in the Book 8 plant ledger as a named motif with its job stated — Cael catalogues it, Vastin owns it, Brom prices it, Oryn finds it — before Ch4 is packeted, and the count stops being a tic question. Do not touch :95, :101 or :127; those three are the motif.

concerns: ':7, in a borrowed room at eighteen with nothing anywhere deciding what he was'. The r1 repair_target explicitly blessed keeping this clause on the Ostrand table ('where it is still true'), and the phrase is the series' shorthand for having no bin rather than for having no proceedings, so it is recorded here rather than raised. But book-06 chapter-17 sits between the cache and the ruling, with a live classification challenge whose whole subject is deciding what he is, and the sentence's nearest relative in the drafted prose is Book 6's closing line, which places it after the Line: 'for the first time in seven years, nothing anywhere was deciding what he was, except him'. If the coordinator wants the clause airtight, it belongs on the crossing, not on the office.

The meadow price is reconciled by construction rather than by arithmetic. ch01.md:13 has Pike naming 'Meadow rate is four a month for a crew that's on my sheet' as the tariff he knocks a winter's lodging down to; :55 now has him saying the meadow is free till the tents fill. The two can be held together — a rate that exists for a crew on the sheet, and ground that costs nothing before the season arrives — but a listener hears 'meadow rate: four a month' in one chapter and 'meadow's free' in the next, seven days apart, and has to do the reconciling. One clause in Ch3 or Ch4 from Pike would close it for good. Separately and still open from r1: STATE_RUNNING records the winter board as 'four a week' where ch01.md:13 says 'four a month', and the ledger's own 'twenty for five months' only works at four a month. The prose is right and the ledger is wrong; this is the coordinator's to fix and is not a defect in either chapter.

The author report's obligation evidence is stale in three places and quotes r1 text against r2 obligations — 'Fifty-six, or near it' at the arrival-catalogue obligation and 'That's not news, Marshal' at the Karis obligation. The report is a navigation aid and never evidence, so this is not raised against the draft, but a coordinator reading the report rather than the diff would conclude two repairs had not landed when in fact both did.

STATE_RUNNING's 'After Chapter 2' block needs three corrections after this repair, none of which the draft can make: it records Vastin as 'Fifty-six or near it' (now fifty-three), and it records 'the record of the last man who tried, very old, filed' as a claim on record, which is the material finding 007 removed from :109 and which no longer exists on the page. The Vastin claims list should carry two items now, not three.

':71, He came through the board' still spends the fixed exchange's own phrase twelve lines before Seln says it at :83. Carried unchanged from r1 and recorded again for the same reason: the turn's first four words arrive already heard, and one substitution at :71 would let the doorway lines land clean.

Lira's crossing is still delivered in past perfect at :123 rather than staged. The repair to finding 002 correctly left :73 alone, so the refusal at the fire survives intact, but the card's 'and sits' still happens off-beat. Recorded, as in r1, because the past-perfect placement does real work.
Vastin's knowledge of the Stair reach is still unsourced at :139. Carried from r1; the chapter supplies a usable answer in its own material and one clause would close it.

The table's decision still runs Seln, Brom, Karis, Oryn, Lira, Cael against the packet scene_shape's 'Karis first … Cael last'. Carried from r1; scene_shape is shape and not obligation, and Cael is still last.

Karis's 'Under every station on the continent. I said so at a table in the autumn.' is spent verbatim at :107 and is scheduled again in the Ch3 card. Flagged for the Ch3 packeting seat, not against this draft. The Ch3 card's staging note — Karis supplies the sub-layer from her own mouth before Vastin speaks — is now half-spent, and STATE_RUNNING's Ch3 block already records the sentence as used there too.

':7, A man built to hold a line' still sits near the prohibition on describing Vastin's Path. Carried from r1: it names nothing and passes, but the Ch4 seat, where Iron Wall is first declared, should know the image is already spent.

Word count is 3,976 against a floor of 3,910 — sixty-six words of margin, six words tighter than r1. Findings 013 and 015 both repair by cutting. If the coordinator wants headroom before Ch3, the concerns above that add (the :71 substitution, a clause sourcing Vastin's Stair knowledge, staging Lira's crossing) are the places to take it.
strengths: The repair is exactly as advertised and the diff proves it. Thirteen changed lines out of a hundred and fifty-five, identical paragraph structure, no reflow, no opportunistic rewriting anywhere in the chapter — this is the revision discipline the craft core asks for, and it is what made a real recheck cheap. Every one of the twelve findings landed at its stated repair_target rather than near it.

Three of the repairs are better than the lines they replaced. ':107, That's not news, Vastin' is colder than 'Marshal' because it uses the name he asked for while telling him he has brought nothing. ':109' ending on 'nobody files a complaint about a wall' is a stronger last line than the three sentences that followed it. ':101, And that was the whole of Brom's price' finishes the paragraph in the idiom the paragraph already established twice. None of these reads like a patch.
